items.label: Tower Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: RECORD QUARTER AND A $2B RUN RATE: Q2 revenue $460M (+11% Qo

set.signal: RECORD QUARTER AND A $2B RUN RATE (CEO Russell Ellwanger / CFO Oren Shirazi): Q2 revenue $460M (+11% QoQ, +24% YoY) with company-record 30% gross margin, 20% operating margin and 20% net margin (EPS $0.80 basic); Q3 guided to $520M mid-range = an annualized revenue run rate ABOVE $2 BILLION. SILICON PHOTONICS: SiPho revenue +>60% QoQ and +>270% YoY to a Q2 annualized run rate ABOVE $680M, TARGETING A $1 BILLION RUN RATE IN Q4 2026 as the capacity expansion is qualified; the full ramp of wafer starts from the $920M SiPho/SiGe capacity program (~50% paid) is anticipated within Q4 2026, creating wafer-start capacity over three times Q2 SiPho shipments, with full financial effect anticipated in Q2 2027. Customer contracts represent ~$1.3 BILLION of 2027 SiPho revenue (even higher growth for 2028); $290M of customer PREPAYMENTS received in Q1, mostly towards 2027 capacity reservations. CEO: Tower is qualified at the lead customers with very strong contracts lasting through 2028, and with very large customers there are 'typically exclusivity agreements on both sides' (for a jointly developed module Tower would request 100% market share). RF infrastructure = 49% of corporate revenue (~43% QoQ, over 140% YoY growth); Fab 7 (300mm Uozu) fully utilized, well above the 85% utilization model. 2028 MODEL RAISED to $3.6B revenue / 45% GM / $1.2B net profit (33%) - $760M revenue above the February model with 67% incremental gross profit.

items.reason: Hedges lost: prepayments were 'mostly' towards 2027 capacity; exclusivity is 'typically' two-way (CEO view, not a stated contract term); 'Demand is CONTRACTED' was editorial; speakers named.
items.evidence: we received $290 million in prepayments from SiPho customers in the first quarter of 2026, mostly towards 2027 capacity reservations

items.label: Tower Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)

set.signal: JAPAN DUAL-TRACK 300MM EXPANSION (CEO Russell Ellwanger; METI-supported): TRACK 1 repurposes the Arai facility (ex-Fab 6) for 300mm SILICON PHOTONICS + advanced packaging and maximizes Fab 7 (Uozu) output - full production readiness expected during Q4 2027 (the driver of the updated 2028 model; the added capacity is 'already requested by and committed to several lead customers'). TRACK 2 constructs an additional 300mm fab adjacent to Fab 7, expected to provide a 4x INCREASE IN JAPANESE 300MM OUTPUT (SiPho, SiGe, advanced optical packaging); the target is everything installed and functioning by Q4 2028, a seamless growth path into 2029; as a minimum Tower intends to add 20,000-25,000 wafers per month of SiPho capacity. Japan chosen for GEOPOLITICAL NEUTRALITY, the Panasonic-heritage R&D workforce and manufacturing-quality culture.

items.reason: Track 2 timing is a 'target' and the 4x an expectation (hedges lost); the funding remark (self-funded, no dilution) is a financing statement and is dropped.
items.evidence: Our target is that everything is installed and functioning by Q4 2028, as stated in the script, that it then provides a seamless growth trajectory into 2029

items.label: Tower Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP: SiPho plugg

set.signal: THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP (CEO Russell Ellwanger): SiPho 800G and 1.6T pluggables 'have, for the most part, already replaced copper for scale-out connections outside the rack'; the next frontier is scale-up, with several Near-Packaged Optics (NPO) deployments planned over the next year and many more in design. On NPO's 2027 share: 'The exact %, I don't yet know. I think it'll be not in the single digits, but in the tens of the percentage of what we'll be shipping, especially in the second half of the year.' NPO itself replaces a pluggable rather than adding content per transceiver, but he agreed a heterogeneous SiGe-on-SiPho structure would be positive, pointing to the die-to-wafer and wafer-to-wafer bonding in the advanced packaging being put in place. Over the next one to two years he expects heterogeneous III-V integration on silicon photonics (integrated lasers, advanced modulators, optical signal processing) to move into high volume; integrated InP lasers should bring several tens of millions of revenue next year (the chip-to-wafer bonding is outsourced now and will be brought in-house; packaging is an enabler, not a separate revenue line). Modulators: a joint OFC press release with Coherent on a 400G modulator in silicon; thin-film lithium niobate and indium phosphide modulators in development. Multi-year IQE epitaxial wafer supply agreement; on the InP crunch, 'we believe that we've addressed that very nicely with the contract with IQE.' SiGe: 100G and 200G per lane products in high volume across all three 200mm fabs (pluggables + LPO/LRO), advancing to NPO and 400G per lane with tighter EIC-PIC co-design, plus strong customer pull for next-generation 300mm SiGe. Image sensors: a sharp surge in machine-vision demand for semiconductor inspection 'driven by the accelerated build-out of DDR and HBM memory assembly lines'.
set.figure: NPO = tens of percent of SiPho shipments, especially H2 2027 (CEO estimate); integrated InP lasers = several tens of millions of revenue next year

items.reason: The NPO share was a hedged CEO estimate ('I think', 'exact % I don't yet know'), mis-quoted as 'in the TENS OF PERCENT'; the IQE fix is 'we believe'; the Coherent modulator is '400G ... in silicon' (no 'per lane'); 'Adjacent read-through' was editorial.
items.evidence: I think it will be significant. The exact %, I don't yet know. I think it'll be not in the single digits, but in the tens of the percentage of what we'll be shipping

items.signal_prefix: Referenced prior joint PR with InnoLight: Tower's best-in-cl

set.signal: CEO Russell Ellwanger, citing an earlier press release with InnoLight: Tower's insertion loss was an enabler for the amount of CW lasers InnoLight needs in the package - 'I believe it was a halving of it. I'd have to go back to the PRs a couple of years ago.' He names best-in-breed insertion loss (fewer and less expensive CW lasers per package) as Tower's biggest differentiator.

items.reason: The halving was a hedged recollection ('I believe', 'I'd have to go back to the PRs'); '~50% fewer' in units is a conversion the source does not state.
items.evidence: We've press released before, it was a press release with InnoLight, about our insertion loss being an enabler to have the amount of CW lasers that they need in the package. I believe it was a halving of it.
